meta.title: Urdu Alphabet
meta.subtitle: 56 letters, marks and pairs · both directions, as two cards per letter
meta.desc: The Urdu alphabet: 56 notes — the forty letters in the order Urdu primers give them (alif madd beside alif, nūn ġunna beside nūn, the two he's and the two ye's), the five marks a dictionary writes over and under the letters and everyday writing leaves out (zabar, zer, peś, taśdīd, jazm), and the eleven breathy pairs a consonant makes with do-caśmī he (بھ, پھ … گھ), which a reader meets on every line. The first deck of the Urdu collection. Urdu is written right to left, and most letters join the next one and change shape as they do, so each card shows the letter alone and then at the start, in the middle and at the end of a word (a letter that never joins the letter after it, such as ا or د, shows two shapes). Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Urdu keeps the spellings of Arabic words with letters that in Urdu sound alike — three s's, four z's, two t's and two h's — so every sound side names its letter, as a speaker does when spelling a word aloud. Every note gives the romanisation the level decks use, the sound described in English words and one everyday word that shows it, with a speaker beside the letter and the word (whether it speaks depends on an Urdu voice being installed on your device). The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them; where English has no equivalent — the breathy consonants, the curled-back ṭ, ḍ and ṛ against the soft dental t and d — the card says what to do with the tongue or the breath instead. The letters are drawn in your device's Urdu typeface, Nastaliq where it has one. Sources: the standard description of Urdu's alphabet and sounds; the example words' romanisations are English Wiktionary's, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0).

fields.Joins: ا ‍ا
fields.Name: الف
fields.Sound: alif: carries the vowel at the start of a word (a, i or u, by the mark above or below it); in the middle or at the end of a word it is a long "a" as in father
fields.Example: ابabnow

fields.Joins: آ ‍آ
fields.Name: الف مد
fields.Sound: ā · alif madd: alif with the wavy madd above: a long "a" as in father at the START of a word
fields.Example: آمāmmango

fields.Joins: ب ب‍ ‍ب‍ ‍ب
fields.Name: بے
fields.Sound: b · be: "b" as in bat
fields.Example: بچہbaccachild

fields.Joins: پ پ‍ ‍پ‍ ‍پ
fields.Name: پے
fields.Sound: p · pe: "p" as in spin — no puff of breath after it
fields.Example: پانیpānīwater

fields.Joins: ت ت‍ ‍ت‍ ‍ت
fields.Name: تے
fields.Sound: t · te: a soft "t" with the tongue against the back of the upper teeth, no puff of breath — the dental t
fields.Example: تینtīnthree

fields.Joins: ٹ ٹ‍ ‍ٹ‍ ‍ٹ
fields.Name: ٹے
fields.Sound: ṭ · ṭe: a hard "t" with the tongue tip curled back to the roof of the mouth — the retroflex t, the little ط above marks it
fields.Example: ٹکٹṭikaṭticket

fields.Joins: ث ث‍ ‍ث‍ ‍ث
fields.Name: ثے
fields.Sound: s · "s" as in sun; written se, in words from Arabic
fields.Example: ثابتsābitproven, firm

fields.Joins: ج ج‍ ‍ج‍ ‍ج
fields.Name: جیم
fields.Sound: j · jīm: "j" as in jam
fields.Example: جگہjagahplace

fields.Joins: چ چ‍ ‍چ‍ ‍چ
fields.Name: چے
fields.Sound: c · che: "ch" as in church, with no puff of breath after it
fields.Example: چائےcāetea

fields.Joins: ح ح‍ ‍ح‍ ‍ح
fields.Name: بڑی حے
fields.Sound: h · "h" as in hand; written baṛī he, "big he", in words from Arabic
fields.Example: حصہhissapart, share

fields.Joins: خ خ‍ ‍خ‍ ‍خ
fields.Name: خے
fields.Sound: x · xe: like the ch of Scottish loch
fields.Example: خوشxuśhappy

fields.Joins: د ‍د
fields.Name: دال
fields.Sound: d · dāl: a soft "d" with the tongue against the upper teeth — the dental d
fields.Example: دنdinday

fields.Joins: ڈ ‍ڈ
fields.Name: ڈال
fields.Sound: ḍ · ḍāl: a hard "d" with the tongue tip curled back — the retroflex d
fields.Example: ڈاکٹرḍākṭardoctor

fields.Joins: ذ ‍ذ
fields.Name: ذال
fields.Sound: z · "z" as in zoo; written zāl, in words from Arabic
fields.Example: ذریعہzariyameans, way

fields.Joins: ر ‍ر
fields.Name: رے
fields.Sound: r · re: a tapped "r", the tongue flicking once behind the teeth, as in Spanish pero
fields.Example: راتrātnight

fields.Joins: ڑ ‍ڑ
fields.Name: ڑے
fields.Sound: ṛ · ṛe: a flap: the tongue tip curls back and flicks forward against the roof of the mouth, between d and r; never starts a word
fields.Example: لڑکاlaṛkāboy

fields.Joins: ز ‍ز
fields.Name: زے
fields.Sound: z · "z" as in zoo; written ze, the everyday z
fields.Example: زبانzabāntongue, language

fields.Joins: ژ ‍ژ
fields.Name: ژے
fields.Sound: ź · źe: "s" as in measure; rare, in words from Persian and French
fields.Example: ٹیلی ویژنṭelī-vīźantelevision

fields.Joins: س س‍ ‍س‍ ‍س
fields.Name: سین
fields.Sound: s · "s" as in sun; written sīn, the everyday s
fields.Example: سالsālyear

fields.Joins: ش ش‍ ‍ش‍ ‍ش
fields.Name: شین
fields.Sound: ś · śīn: "sh" as in shop
fields.Example: شہرśahrcity

fields.Joins: ص ص‍ ‍ص‍ ‍ص
fields.Name: صاد
fields.Sound: s · "s" as in sun; written su'ād, in words from Arabic
fields.Example: صبحsubhmorning

fields.Joins: ض ض‍ ‍ض‍ ‍ض
fields.Name: ضاد
fields.Sound: z · "z" as in zoo; written zu'ād, in words from Arabic
fields.Example: ضرورتzarūratneed

fields.Joins: ط ط‍ ‍ط‍ ‍ط
fields.Name: طوئے
fields.Sound: t · the soft dental "t"; written to'e, in words from Arabic
fields.Example: طرفtarafside, direction

fields.Joins: ظ ظ‍ ‍ظ‍ ‍ظ
fields.Name: ظوئے
fields.Sound: z · "z" as in zoo; written zo'e, in words from Arabic
fields.Example: ظاہرzāhirclear, evident

fields.Joins: ع ع‍ ‍ع‍ ‍ع
fields.Name: عین
fields.Sound: ' · 'ain: in Urdu mostly silent, colouring the vowel beside it (a throat sound in Arabic)
fields.Example: عورت'auratwoman

fields.Joins: غ غ‍ ‍غ‍ ‍غ
fields.Name: غین
fields.Sound: ġ · ġain: a gargled "g", like the French r
fields.Example: غلطġalatwrong

fields.Joins: ف ف‍ ‍ف‍ ‍ف
fields.Name: فے
fields.Sound: f · fe: "f" as in fan
fields.Example: فونfūnphone

fields.Joins: ق ق‍ ‍ق‍ ‍ق
fields.Name: قاف
fields.Sound: q · qāf: a "k" made further back, in the throat (from Arabic)
fields.Example: قلمqalampen

fields.Joins: ک ک‍ ‍ک‍ ‍ک
fields.Name: کاف
fields.Sound: k · kāf: "k" as in skin — no puff of breath after it
fields.Example: کتابkitābbook

fields.Joins: گ گ‍ ‍گ‍ ‍گ
fields.Name: گاف
fields.Sound: g · gāf: "g" as in go
fields.Example: گاؤںgāõvillage

fields.Joins: ل ل‍ ‍ل‍ ‍ل
fields.Name: لام
fields.Sound: l · lām: "l" as in leaf, light and clear
fields.Example: لالlālred

fields.Joins: م م‍ ‍م‍ ‍م
fields.Name: میم
fields.Sound: m · mīm: "m" as in man
fields.Example: ماںmā̃mother

fields.Joins: ن ن‍ ‍ن‍ ‍ن
fields.Name: نون
fields.Sound: n · nūn: "n" as in name
fields.Example: نامnāmname

fields.Joins: ‍ں
fields.Name: نون غنہ
fields.Sound: nūn ġunna, n without its dot: the vowel before it is said through the nose, as in French bon; only at the end of a word
fields.Example: ہاںhā̃yes

fields.Joins: و ‍و
fields.Name: واؤ
fields.Sound: v · vā'o: "v", softer than English v, close to w; or a vowel — ū as in food, o as in go (one pure vowel), au as in law
fields.Example: وقتvaqttime

fields.Joins: ہ ہ‍ ‍ہ‍ ‍ہ
fields.Name: چھوٹی ہے
fields.Sound: h · "h" as in hand; written choṭī he, "little he", the everyday h; at the end of a word often a short "a" (بچہ bacca)
fields.Example: ہاتھhāthhand

fields.Joins: ھ ھ‍ ‍ھ‍ ‍ھ
fields.Name: دو چشمی ہے
fields.Sound: h · do-caśmī he, "two-eyed he": a breath after the consonant before it, which it never leaves — it writes the aspirated pairs below
fields.Example: بھائیbhāībrother

fields.Name: ہمزہ
fields.Sound: hamza: a break between two vowels that meet, each said in turn; written alone or above a letter (ئ ؤ ۂ)
fields.Example: کئیkaīseveral

fields.Joins: ی ی‍ ‍ی‍ ‍ی
fields.Name: چھوٹی یے
fields.Sound: y · choṭī ye: "y" as in yes; or a vowel — ī as in see, e as in cake (one pure vowel), ai; at the end of a word ī
fields.Example: یادyādmemory

fields.Joins: ‍ے
fields.Name: بڑی یے
fields.Sound: e · baṛī ye, "big ye": only at the end of a word, said e as in cake or ai
fields.Example: آگےāgeforward

fields.Name: زبر
fields.Sound: a · zabar, the stroke above: a short neutral "a" as in about after the letter
fields.Example: اَبabnow

fields.Name: زیر
fields.Sound: i · zer, the stroke below: a short "i" as in bit after the letter
fields.Example: دِنdinday

fields.Name: پیش
fields.Sound: u · peś, the little و above: a short "u" as in put after the letter
fields.Example: خُوشxuśhappy

fields.Name: تشدید
fields.Sound: taśdīd, the little w above: the letter is doubled, held twice as long
fields.Example: بَچّہbaccachild

fields.Name: جزم
fields.Sound: jazm, the little circle above: NO vowel after the letter
fields.Example: وَقْتvaqttime

fields.Name: بھ
fields.Sound: bh · bh: "b" followed by a breathy h, as in the middle of clubhouse
fields.Example: بھائیbhāībrother

fields.Name: پھ
fields.Sound: ph · ph: "p" with a strong puff of breath, as in pit said firmly — never the f of phone
fields.Example: پھلphalfruit

fields.Name: تھ
fields.Sound: th · the soft dental t with a strong puff of breath — never the th of thin
fields.Example: تھوڑاthoṛāa little

fields.Name: ٹھ
fields.Sound: ṭh · ṭh: the curled-back ṭ with a strong puff of breath
fields.Example: ٹھیکṭhīkall right, fine

fields.Name: جھ
fields.Sound: jh · jh: "j" followed by a breathy h
fields.Example: جھوٹjhūṭa lie

fields.Name: چھ
fields.Sound: ch · ch: "ch" with a strong puff of breath, as in the middle of church-hill
fields.Example: چھوٹاchoṭāsmall

fields.Name: دھ
fields.Sound: dh · dh: the soft dental d followed by a breathy h
fields.Example: دودھdūdhmilk

fields.Name: ڈھ
fields.Sound: ḍh · ḍh: the curled-back ḍ followed by a breathy h
fields.Example: ڈھونڈناḍhūnḍnāto look for

fields.Name: ڑھ
fields.Sound: ṛh · ṛh: the flap ṛ followed by a breathy h; never starts a word
fields.Example: پڑھناpaṛhnāto read, to study

fields.Name: کھ
fields.Sound: kh · kh: "k" with a strong puff of breath, as in kit said firmly
fields.Example: کھاناkhānāfood; to eat

fields.Name: گھ
fields.Sound: gh · gh: "g" followed by a breathy h, as in the middle of doghouse
fields.Example: گھرgharhouse, home
